key_insight: β-TeO3 is predicted to be a wide-band-gap n-type semiconductor with exceptionally high work functions, reaching about 8 eV, making it promising for charge-injection and transparent-electrode roles.
engineering_relevance: Its defect and surface chemistry suggest it could serve in photovoltaic and light-emitting device stacks, but performance depends strongly on controlling oxygen vacancies and chemical potential during growth.
method: First-principles calculations of the electronic structure and defect energetics.
Assessment of point defects including H, Li, Na, Cu, Mg, Zn, F, and oxygen vacancies.
Work-function evaluation across low-index nonpolar surfaces.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a band gap above 3 eV, shallow-donor behavior for several impurities, and surface-dependent work functions up to ~8 eV, with oxygen vacancies lowering the work function.
watch_item: Surface oxygen-vacancy formation can reduce the ultrahigh work function, so growth and post-processing must tightly control oxygen chemical potential.
paper_title: Tellurium trioxide as an n-type wide-gap semiconductor with ultrahigh work functions from first principles
